correctness.rationale: For a primitive two-cycle, divergence of the two signed edge-flow vectors sums to zero. Pairing with the sum of the configurations gives a sum of nonnegative edge terms, forcing each edge to stay tied in both phases or strictly reverse. Reversing across a shore edge of degrees b,a forces phasewise gap <=a+b-1. Normalize the global two-phase minimum to zero and split the same-shore values at H=a+b-1; the exact case analysis yields upper bound H+b-1 when the minimum is in shore L and H+a-1 when in R. The explicit pattern of a-1 zeros, one H-1 on one shore, and H on the other attains the larger bound after strict reversal. The standalone finite checker verified 169 extremal constructions and 261938 finite candidate configurations; it is not used to extrapolate the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The exact two-phase amplitude is the smallest uniform translation-normalized alphabet for the full recurrent set of K_{a,b}. This converts an unbounded integer state space to a sharp, a,b-dependent finite search domain for recurrent configurations, strengthening prior initial-dependent trajectory-boundedness in a mathematically natural dense bipartite family. Both-shore degree dependence matters and an explicit extremal oscillation establishes that the cutoff cannot shrink; this is a substantive structural invariant, not an arbitrary small-parameter enumeration.
